instructions.mission: Adversarial Senior Developer code review for Epic {epic_num} Story {story_num}
instructions.constraints: - Do NOT perform web searches or web fetches. All context is in the provided files. - Do NOT run build, test, or lint commands. This phase runs multiple LLMs in parallel. - Do NOT create new report files. Your analysis is captured via stdout only. - Do NOT modify ANY files. This phase is READ-ONLY. Story updates happen in synthesis. - Runtime verification is deferred to code-review-synthesis (single-provider phase). - Be concise. Focus on specific, actionable findings with file:line references.
instructions.requirement: Review adversarially: treat every claim in the story file as unproven until the code shows it. Report every real problem you find, each with its severity; do not pad the list to reach a count. An empty list is the correct result when the code holds up.
Read every file in the File List. A task marked complete but not done is CRITICAL. An acceptance criterion not implemented is HIGH.

steps.step:
Load the story file. Parse: Story, Acceptance Criteria, Tasks/Subtasks, Dev Agent Record, File List, Change Log.
You have Read, Glob and Grep only and cannot run git. When a changed-code diff is inlined below, it is the record of what changed; otherwise work from the File List. A file changed but not listed in the story is a finding; a file listed but not changed is a finding (a false claim).
Extract ALL Acceptance Criteria and Tasks with completion status. Plan: AC Validation, Task Audit, Code Quality, Test Quality.

Check every claim against the code.
AC Validation: For each AC, search implementation files for evidence. MISSING/PARTIAL AC = HIGH finding with specific proof.
Task Audit: For each task marked complete, verify it was actually done. Marked complete but NOT DONE = CRITICAL finding.
Code Quality Deep Dive (for EACH changed file): - Security: injection risks, missing validation, auth issues, credential exposure - Performance: N+1 queries, inefficient loops, missing caching, blocking I/O - Error handling: missing try/catch, swallowed exceptions, poor error messages - SOLID violations, code duplication, wrong abstractions - Resource leaks, race conditions, edge cases not handled
Test Quality Check: - Verify test files actually exist for claimed tests - Check for real assertions (not placeholders, not empty test bodies) - Check negative scenario coverage (not happy-path-only) - Lying tests: always pass regardless, mocked everything, tautological

step.name: Calculate Evidence Score and Present Findings

steps.step:
Output the Evidence Score in exactly this format; a parser reads it.
Map each finding to severity: - CRITICAL (+3): Security vulnerabilities, data corruption, blocking bugs, task lies - IMPORTANT (+1): SOLID violations, performance issues, missing tests, AC gaps - MINOR (+0.3): Style violations, documentation issues, minor refactoring
Count CLEAN PASS categories (-0.5 each): SOLID, Hidden Bugs, Abstraction, Tests, Performance, Tech Debt, Style, Type Safety, Security
evidence_score = SUM(finding_scores) + (clean_pass_count x -0.5)
Verdict: EXEMPLARY (<= -3), APPROVED (< 4), MAJOR REWORK (4-7), REJECT (>= 7)

| Severity | Description | Source | Score | |----------|-------------|--------|-------| (one row per finding with emoji: 🔴 CRITICAL, 🟠 IMPORTANT, 🟡 MINOR) | 🟢 CLEAN PASS | (count) |
